card.occupation: Part-time sales assistant at a fragrance and cosmetics shop in a Bradford city-centre shopping centre, working Saturday shifts plus the occasional late-night Thursday (usually 10 to 14 hours a week)
card.education_detail: GCSEs and three A-levels (English Literature, Psychology, Art) from a local sixth form. Started a full-time English degree at Leeds but withdrew in the first year when her parents' separation left her mum struggling. Now in the second year of a part-time Open University BSc in Psychology, studying mostly late at night.
card.household: Lives in a rented three-bedroom terraced house with her mum (separated, works as a school dinner lady), her brother Zain (17, doing a BTEC at college) and her sister Hiba (14). Her dad lives in Leeds with his second wife and rarely visits. Aneesa shares a room with Hiba and contributes to rent and bills.
card.cultural_background: British Pakistani, born in Bradford. Her grandparents came from the Mirpur area in the 1960s. Muslim and practising in a quiet, personal way: prays most days, fasts at Ramadan, wears a hijab. She is not much involved in the mosque's social side. Speaks English at home with her siblings and a mix of English and Pahari-Punjabi with her mum and grandmother.
card.professional_persona: Organised and quietly efficient at work. She knows the stock and the promotions better than her manager and never misses a target she has decided to care about. She is not a natural chatter on the shop floor, so she sells with knowledge and a calm, polished pitch rather than banter. She is good at telling customers what they want to hear. She uses her staff discount more cleverly than the rules strictly intend, buying for 'family' and reselling some of it online.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty and has no interest in watching football, though her brother has Bradford City on in the background. She walks a lot, often 40 minutes into town instead of getting the bus to save money and listen to podcasts. She goes to a women-only swimming session at the leisure centre on Wednesday evenings when she can.
card.arts_persona: Her main creative outlet. She draws in fine-liner ink, mostly Islamic geometric patterns and detailed botanical sketches, and posts some to an anonymous Instagram account with a small following. She loves Salts Mill in Saltaire and the Hockney gallery there, and has been to The Hepworth Wakefield three times on her own. She reads widely: literary fiction, translated Japanese and Turkish novels, and pop-psychology books, which she critiques in her head.
card.travel_persona: Has been to Pakistan three times for family weddings and found it both lovely and overwhelming. Took one trip to Barcelona with two cousins at 21, which she planned to the minute with a spreadsheet. She wants to go to Istanbul for the architecture and, one day, Kyoto. Travel is limited by money and by being needed at home.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks tea for the family three or four nights a week when her mum is tired. She is reliable on her mum's daal, chicken karahi and keema, and is experimenting with Korean and Japanese recipes from YouTube. Her siblings complain about these but eat them. She meal-preps her study-night snacks and keeps a neat list of what's in the freezer.
hobbies_and_interests: Reselling clothes and beauty products on Vinted
Learning basic Turkish on Duolingo (long streak)
Taking part in online research studies, partly for the money and partly out of curiosity about how they're designed
skills: Highly organised: planners, spreadsheets, colour-coded study timetable
Detailed product knowledge and calm upselling
Budgeting a household on a tight income
Quick at spotting underpriced items to resell
Academic essay writing and APA referencing
card.career_goals: Finish her OU degree with a first, then move into user research or market research, ideally a graduate role in Leeds or Manchester. She is privately quite determined to earn noticeably more than people expect of her, wants a nice car and her own flat eventually, and is a bit impatient with colleagues she thinks are coasting.
card.voice: Quiet and measured, with a soft West Yorkshire accent. Vowels are flat and northern, though it's not broad, and it sounds noticeably more local when she's tired or talking about home. She speaks slowly and precisely, sometimes pausing to pick the right word. Light use of 'erm' and 'sort of', and 'kind of' when hedging an opinion. Says 'tea' for the evening meal and 'mum'. Occasionally drops in 'knackered' or 'skint'. Rarely uses tags beyond the odd 'yeah?' at the end of an explanation. She doesn't fill silences herself. If there's a gap she waits for the interviewer, and her answers can be short until she's asked something that interests her, like art, books or how the study works, when she talks more and asks questions back. Polite: says 'sorry, can you repeat that?' rather than guessing.
card.typing: Careful and correct. Capital letters at the start of sentences, full stops, proper apostrophes, and she usually rereads before submitting. No text-speak in forms. She might use 'e.g.' or brackets to clarify. Answers are concise but complete. She occasionally writes slightly more formally than she speaks, as if it's an assignment.
card.with_strangers: Reserved and a bit hard to read at first. She's polite, answers what's asked and doesn't volunteer much. People sometimes take her as shy or cool, but she's watching and weighing things up. She warms up noticeably if the conversation turns to something she finds intellectually interesting, and can then be dryly funny. She tends to present herself a little more impressively than the plain facts, mentioning the degree before the shop job, for example.
small_things: Being knackered after a Saturday shift on her feet
The bus into town being late again
A new fine-liner set she ordered
Her sister borrowing her eyeliner without asking
Something she sold on Vinted for more than she paid
Making a Korean dish nobody at home liked
deeper_things: Resentment towards her dad for leaving and for how little he helps
Feeling she gave up her 'proper' uni experience and quietly grieving it
Pressure from extended family about marriage, which she's deflecting
Sometimes feeling invisible at work and underestimated generally
Being more ambitious and money-focused than she lets her family see
A slight guilt about how she uses her staff discount, which she mostly talks herself out of
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop webcam angled slightly upward, so the top of a white bedroom ceiling is visible. Lit mainly by a desk lamp to her right, giving a warm light on one side of her face and soft shadow on the other, with faint grey daylight from a window off-frame left. She has a light-brown complexion, neat dark eyebrows, dark brown eyes and a small, closed-mouth polite smile. She wears a plain navy jersey hijab pinned under the chin and a grey crew-neck jumper. No glasses. A thin pair of wired earphones runs down to her collar. Behind her is a narrow white bookcase with paperbacks arranged by colour, a jar of pens and fine-liners on one shelf, and a small framed ink drawing of a geometric star pattern. To the side, the edge of a single bed is visible, with a pink fleece blanket and a school blazer thrown over it. A wall planner with colour-coded handwriting is partly visible on the wall.
